interview_question: How would you measure the success of a new "Save for later" button in a news app?
answer: I'd track articles saved per weekly user and how many saved articles get opened within a week. The second matters most. The goal is to get people reading more.
criterion_or_rubric: Names at least two specific user actions, such as saving an article and coming back to read it
claude_note: Goal comes after the metrics. Actions are only implied inside the metric names. Pick has no reason.

interview_question: How would you measure the success of an AI that drafts replies for agents in a customer support tool?
answer: Rather than average CSAT, which can rise just because the AI only gets easy tickets, I'd count tickets resolved using an AI draft each week. I'd hold reopen rate flat as we expand, so faster replies don't come at the cost of wrong ones. If agents rewrite most drafts from scratch, that tells us they don't trust them.
criterion_or_rubric: Includes override rate: how often agents heavily edit or discard the AI's draft
claude_note: Describes the override signal (rewriting drafts from scratch) without calling it a tracked rate.

interview_question: How would you measure the success of an AI feature that writes product descriptions for online sellers?
answer: Looking at sellers on our marketplace over the first month, I'd track descriptions published without edits, listings per seller, and revenue.
criterion_or_rubric: Names a business metric separately, such as cost per description or sales on listings with AI descriptions
claude_note: Revenue is named, but in the same list as the secondary metrics, not separately.

interview_question: How would you measure the success of an AI that drafts replies for agents in a customer support tool?
answer: North Star, absolute count, guardrails, override rate, SIGNAL, trust, hallucination rate, escalations, cost per query.

interview_question: How would you measure the success of Spotify's Discover Weekly playlist?
answer: I would track weekly listeners and songs saved from the playlist um and also average listening time on it the most important is songs saved because saving means they liked it um and I think also skips would matter like if people skip a lot in the first few seconds that is a bad sign and I would compare this week to last week
criterion_or_rubric: Names specific user actions (opening the playlist, playing, saving tracks) with a countable metric for each
claude_note: No goal. Actions only implied by the metrics.

interview_question: How would you measure the success of an AI trip planner that builds travel itineraries?
answer: okay I would focus on business travelers in europe for the first quarter um and the key numbers are booking revenue and the cost per itinerary because the planner has to pay for itself and I would want both of those to move in the right direction every month um because at the end of the day the planner needs to make money and stay cheap to run so those are the numbers leadership will ask about first in every review
criterion_or_rubric:
5 excellent: Clarifies scope, anchors on a count-based North Star, separates actionable secondary metrics from business metrics, sets an AI guardrail, and gives a tracking plan with method and cadence for the key metrics
4 good: Covers most of C-NABGT, but the tracking plan is vague ("we'd instrument it") or secondary and business metrics are blurred
3 fair: Reasonable metrics but no scope and no tracking plan, or a ratio North Star with no count or caveat
1-2 poor: Generic engagement or satisfaction with no definitions
claude_note: Scope plus business metrics only; could be 2.

interview_question: Task completion rate for your AI customer-support chatbot fell from 70% to 58% this month. How would you investigate?
answer: I would check whether the model got updated silently because that is the most common cause and look at whether we moved to a cheaper model to save money which can make answers worse and also check latency because a slow bot makes people give up halfway um and once we know which one it is we can fix it pretty quickly and let the support team know what happened so they can tell customers if they ask about it
criterion_or_rubric: Adds the AI layer without being prompted, and separates model-layer from application-layer causes
claude_note: Model-layer cause only, with no application-layer split.
